# Aunt Josephine

## Overview

- **Age:** presumed seventy  <sub>[v1 CHAPTER XIX. A Concert, a Catastrophe, and a Confession P54](../source/v01-c19.md#nw-v01-c19-p0054)</sub>
- **Gender:** female  <sub>[v1 CHAPTER XIX. A Concert, a Catastrophe, and a Confession P77](../source/v01-c19.md#nw-v01-c19-p0077)</sub>
- **Status:** alive  _(assumed)_
- **Family:** [Diana](../character/diana.md) (relative)

## Appearance

Aunt Josephine is a thin, prim, and rigid woman who wears gold-rimmed glasses. She can often be found knitting fiercely by the fire.

_Sources: [v1 CHAPTER XIX. A Concert, a Catastrophe, and a Confession P77](../source/v01-c19.md#nw-v01-c19-p0077)_

## Personality

Aunt Josephine is known for being exceptionally prim and proper. She maintains a strict demeanor and is quick to scold others dreadfully when her standards are not met.

_Sources: [v1 CHAPTER XIX. A Concert, a Catastrophe, and a Confession P54](../source/v01-c19.md#nw-v01-c19-p0054)_

## Traits

## History

Aunt Josephine, a resident of [Charlottetown](../codex/places.md#charlottetown), was visiting [Orchard Slope](../codex/places.md#orchard-slope) when [Anne Shirley](../character/anne-shirley.md) and [Diana Barry](../character/di.md) unexpectedly leaped onto her in a spare-room bed. Though initially furious and threatening to cancel Diana's music lessons, [Miss Barry](../character/miss-barry.md) was won over when [Anne](../character/anne.md) bravely visited her to explain the mistake and take full responsibility. Touched by Anne's sincerity, [Miss Barry](../character/miss-barry.md) decided to prolong her stay in [Avonlea](../codex/places.md#avonlea), and the two formed a firm friendship. She later sent [Anne](../character/anne.md) a pair of dainty kid slippers for [Christmas](../codex/places.md#merry-christmas) and eventually invited both [Anne](../character/anne.md) and [Diana](../character/diana.md) to her [Charlottetown](../codex/places.md#charlottetown) estate, [Beechwood](../codex/places.md#beechwood), where she hosted them for several days of [Exhibition](../codex/places.md#exhibition) festivities and town entertainments.

_Sources: [v1 CHAPTER XIX. A Concert, a Catastrophe, and a Confession P2](../source/v01-c19.md#nw-v01-c19-p0002), [v1 CHAPTER XIX. ## Quotes

> “I’m afraid my imagination is a little rusty—it’s so long since I used it,” she said. “I dare say your claim to sympathy is just as strong as mine. It all depends on the way we look at it. Sit down here and tell me about yourself.”
>
> — Aunt Josephine — [v1 CHAPTER XIX. A Concert, a Catastrophe, and a Confession P88](../source/v01-c19.md#nw-v01-c19-p0088)

> “I’ve made up my mind to stay simply for the sake of getting better acquainted with that Anne-girl,” she said frankly. “She amuses me, and at my time of life an amusing person is a rarity.”
>
> — Aunt Josephine — [v1 CHAPTER XIX. A Concert, a Catastrophe, and a Confession P92](../source/v01-c19.md#nw-v01-c19-p0092)

> "Mercy, child, how you have grown! You’re taller than I am, I declare. And you’re ever so much better-looking than you used to be, too. But I dare say you know that without being told."
>
> — Aunt Josephine — [v1 CHAPTER XXIX. An Epoch in Anne’s Life P18](../source/v01-c29.md#nw-v01-c29-p0018)

> "Remember, you Anne-girl, when you come to town you’re to visit me and I’ll put you in my very sparest spare-room bed to sleep."
>
> — Aunt Josephine — [v1 CHAPTER XIX. A Concert, a Catastrophe, and a Confession P96](../source/v01-c19.md#nw-v01-c19-p0096)

> "Oh, I must, hey? I rather think Diana did her share of the jumping at least. Such carryings on in a respectable house!"
>
> — Aunt Josephine — [v1 CHAPTER XIX. A Concert, a Catastrophe, and a Confession P82](../source/v01-c19.md#nw-v01-c19-p0082)

## Relationships

### [Diana](../character/diana.md) · [the relationship](../relationships/aunt-josephine--diana.md)

Aunt Josephine is Diana's grand-aunt. Their relationship is initially strained when [Diana](../character/diana.md) and [Anne](../character/anne.md) accidentally leap onto her in a spare bed during a game, furious [Miss Barry](../character/miss-barry.md) by the disruption and threatening to cancel Diana's music lessons as punishment. However, after [Anne](../character/anne.md) intervenes to apologize and reconcile with her, Aunt Josephine maintains a fond connection with [Diana](../character/diana.md), later sending her dainty slippers to give to [Anne](../character/anne.md) for [Christmas](../codex/places.md#merry-christmas) and inviting both girls to spend several days at her grand [Charlottetown](../codex/places.md#charlottetown) estate for the [Exhibition](../codex/places.md#exhibition).
